description:
CAPABILITY CLASS -> REASONING EFFORT. The third dimension, beside CLASS -> MODEL (routing/capabilities.json) and MODEL FAMILY -> SHIM (routing/shims.json), and kept here for the same reason they are kept apart: one file, one decision. How much thinking a class gets is a property of the WORK, so it is one vocabulary here and not a column per provider; how a provider SPELLS it is that provider's adapter (tools/fabric/routing.py), and whether a given model admits a level is the adapter's per-model table. Effort exists as a routed value because it was not one: every model the fabric had pinned happened to default to `high`, and Opus 5.5 was the first that did not — moving code-high to it would have dropped every session a level with no commit and nothing to review (docs/live-checks/2026-09-23-opus-5-5.md). A model's own default is never the fabric's decision. A provider may also hold a level CHOSEN for it (providers.

.chosen lists the classes): a decision, with its note, that the model must take as it is — the Codex engine's code-review at high (the owner, 2026-10-12) — beside the acknowledgements, which record what a model's narrower set makes of the class's own level.
levels_note: Ordered, least to most. The union of the vendors' scales, not any one vendor's: Anthropic admits low..max, OpenAI all seven, xAI none..xhigh, DeepSeek low/high/max, GLM-5.3-Flash low/high/max. A level is an ORDINAL, never a magnitude — no vendor asserts that its `high` means another's, and neither does this file. What a class asks for is fitted to what its model admits, by the fabric, before the request leaves: the vendor's own documented mapping where there is one (in either direction); else clamped DOWN to the nearest level below; and a request below the model's floor is raised UP to that floor, since sending nothing would hand the vendor its default (tools/fabric/routing.py effort_for): the vendors disagree on the failure mode (OpenAI returns 400, xAI and Claude Code clamp silently, GLM-5.3-Flash errors, DeepSeek remaps), and a routing decision must not mean two different things depending on who serves it.
session_note: A level, or a capability class whose level to take — as routing/profiles.json's own `session` may name a class. Every session thinks at medium (the owner, 2026-09-25), as every class does, so the level is named directly. A layer that gives one agent's session another model does not move its level: architect-cto-01's session is Fable 5.1 (routing/profiles.json) and thinks at medium too.

notes.all: No override: every class asks medium. code-high, code-plan and code-review are Opus 5.5, whose own default medium is; code-low is Haiku 5.5 (the owner, 2026-10-07) and code-medium Sonnet 5.5 (the owner, 2026-09-29), both of which admit medium and served it when read back (docs/live-checks/2026-10-07-haiku-5-5.md, docs/live-checks/2026-09-29-sonnet-5-5.md). Before, code-low rode Haiku 4.5, which takes no effort, and code-medium asked Sonnet 5 for less than its default high.

notes.code-low: code-low asks for medium (the owner, 2026-09-25: every class at medium); z-ai/glm-5.3-flash distinguishes only low/high/max, and the nearest level at or below medium is low, so low is what it serves. Written down because that is a level lost, and a lost level is a commit.
notes.all: Every other class asks medium and its broker model has no medium: z-ai/glm-5.2 (code-medium) and deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro-0813 (code-high, code-plan, code-review) are served high, the vendors' documented mapping, one level above what the class asks. Nothing is lost there, so no override. On the broker code-high, code-plan and code-review therefore differ in neither model nor effort. That is true of today's broker column, not a property of the design.

notes.code-review: high, chosen for this provider (the owner, 2026-10-12, in the coordinator's session), not fitted: the review class asks medium elsewhere, and gpt-6.1-sol takes medium as it is. On Codex the owner chose high for the contrarian reviewer — a second engine is there to find what the first missed, and a review reads a whole change — and because Codex's own default on the ChatGPT plan was `none` (a `codex exec` on the owner's team plan printed "reasoning effort: none", 2026-10-12), so sending no level would hand the review the least thinking there is. Listed in `chosen`, so routing.py check judges it as a decision the model must take exactly rather than as an acknowledged downgrade. It reaches Codex as -c model_reasoning_effort="high" (tools/fabric/routing.py effort_spelling), on fabric-review --engine codex --gateway chatgpt; the environment's gateway sends a level only when --effort or AGENT_FABRIC_CODEX_EFFORT asks for one (review of #224, F2).
